concerns.text: T009 instructs to 'append them to features.csv' — an in-place modification of a derived data file. Constitution III states 'No data may be modified in place; every transformation MUST produce a new file with a documented derivation.' The fallback must write to a new filename (e.g., features_augmented.csv) with the derivation documented; the task as written bakes a constitution violation into the deliverable.

concerns.location: tasks.md:T002 Output vs spec.md:SC-005 / US-1 Acceptance Scenario 1
concerns.text: T002 states 'target ≥500 rows; a smaller real result is acceptable and must be reported honestly.' SC-005 and US-1's acceptance scenario require 'at least 500 perovskite compositions.' This is a silent narrowing of an acceptance criterion — the spec nowhere authorizes continuing below 500. Either amend the spec to stage this (explicitly documenting <500 as a limitation with justification) or make the task enforce the criterion; a task cannot unilaterally relax it.

FR-012's trigger reads 'do not achieve RMSE ≤ 0.5 eV or R² ≥ 70 %' (literal reading: fallback only when BOTH fail), while T008 evaluates 'RMSE > 0.5 eV OR R² < 0.70' (fallback when EITHER fails). The task's interpretation is stricter, not weaker, but the artifacts contradict each other on a MUST-level requirement; reconcile to one interpretation across spec, plan, and T008/T009 so the fallback trigger is unambiguous.

T008's verification requires performance.json to 'validate against the ENTIRE contracts/model_performance.schema.yaml, including ... feature_importances', but feature_importances are only populated by T009, which depends on T008. As ordered, T008's own acceptance check can never pass — a verification step that contradicts the dependency graph. Scope T008's check to the sections it produces (cv_metrics, test_metrics, bootstrap_ci, paired_ttest) and move the full-schema validation to T009/T010.
